title: Pregnancy Food Safety Analysis: Sushi, Salads, BBQ, and Cheese Boards
excerpt: A pregnancy food safety analysis of international favorites like sushi, salads, BBQ, and cheese boards
content:
## Introduction
When it comes to pregnancy, choosing safe and nutritious food is crucial. Pregnant women need to be careful when selecting international dishes like sushi, salads, BBQ, and cheese boards. In this article, we will analyze the food safety of these dishes for pregnant women.

## Food Safety Analysis
According to the CDC and NHS, pregnant women should avoid eating raw sushi and sashimi due to the risk of bacterial and parasitic infections. However, cooked or pasteurized sushi and sashimi are safe to eat. Salads can also be a good option, but pregnant women need to be careful when selecting ingredients and ensuring that all ingredients are washed and pasteurized.

BBQ and cheese boards can also be a good option, but pregnant women need to be careful when selecting the type of meat and cheese. According to the EPA/FDA, pregnant women should avoid eating raw or undercooked meat and soft cheese that has not been pasteurized. However, cooked or pasteurized BBQ and cheese are safe to eat.

## Nutrient Combination
To ensure that pregnant women get enough nutrients, it's essential to combine international dishes with nutrient-rich ingredients. For example, pregnant women can combine sushi with omega-3 rich fish, salads with leafy greens and fruits, BBQ with lean meat and vegetables, and cheese boards with fruits and vegetables.

## Foods to Avoid
Pregnant women should avoid eating the following foods:
* Raw sushi and sashimi
* Raw or undercooked meat
* Soft cheese that has not been pasteurized
* Salads with unwashed and unpasteurized ingredients

## Practical Tips
To ensure food safety and nutrition for pregnant women, it's essential to:
* Choose cooked or pasteurized international dishes
* Combine international dishes with nutrient-rich ingredients
* Avoid eating foods that should be avoided
* Consult a [meal planner](/blog/planner) to get a safe and nutritious eating plan

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about food safety and nutrition, they should seek help from a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. To learn more about prenatal nutrition, pregnant women can visit our [prenatal nutrition category](/blog/prenatal-nutrition) page.
